Copper/Photoredox-Catalyzed Regioselective 1,4-Addition to 
1,3-Enynes: A Convenient Access to Perfluoroalkylated Allenes 
Ya Chen,*,a Quanyuan Wang,a Keyi Peng,a Lilei Cheng,a Ziyi She,a and Guo-Jun Deng*,a,b 
a Key Laboratory for Green Organic Synthesis and Application of Hunan Province, Key Laboratory of Environmentally Friendly Chemistry

Regioselectivity 
Comprehensive Summary  
 
A general and broadly applicable copper and photoredox  dual-catalyzed multicomponent 1,4 -perfluoroalkylcyanation of 1,3 -enynes 
has been developed. This protocol enjoys success with high regioselectivity, mild reaction conditions, and excellent function al-group 
tolerance, allowing the facile synthesis of struc turally diverse perfluoroalkylated allenes from readily available fluoroalkyl halides, 
1,3-enynes and TMSCN in a one -pot manner . A reasonable mechanism has been proposed according to a series of control experi-
ments.

Background and Originality Content 
The incorporation of a fluorine atom or fluorinated groups in -
to organic frameworks can significantly alter their physicochemical 
properties and bioactivity, increasing their applicability as phar -
maceuticals, agrochemicals, or building blocks for organic materi -
als.[1] As a consequence, the development of efficient fluoroalkyl -
ation methods has attracted notable attention in drug discovery 
and modern organic chemistry. [2] In contrast to the recent signifi -
cant progress in the fluoroalkylation of conventional alkenes and 
alkynes, which provid es an access to the corresponding fluoroal -
kanes or fluoroalkenes, [3] efficient routes for the synthesis of 
fluoroalkylated allenes are less abundant. In recent years, di - and 
trisubstituted trifluoromethyl-allenes were successfully assembled 
by elimination, [4] isomerization,[5] rearrangements,[6] and S N2' 
reactions[7] from alkynyl or alkenyl substrates bearing a CF3 group. 
Alternative access to CF 3-allenes relied on the trifl uoromethyla-
tion of propargylic derivatives with “CuCF3” as a nucleophile. [8] 
Despite these important achievements, there are suffering limita -
tions with the need for the prefunctionalized substrates, which 
are generally associated with low efficiency and poor atom 
economy. On the other hand, the installation of other fluorinated 
groups, such as perfluoroalkyl and functionalized difluorometh -
ylene into allenes, particularly tetra -substituted allenes, are still 
remaining challenges.[9] 
Multicomponent reactio ns (MCRs) represent an appealing 
strategy for the construction of multiple carbon-carbon or carbon- 
heteroatom bonds from easily available feedstocks in one simple 
operation.[10] Recently, the feasibility of MCRs in the assembly of 
multi-substituted allenes has been manifested through transition - 
metal-catalyzed difunctionalization of 1,3-enynes,[11] especially via 
radical-involved pathways. [12] In this regard, diverse kinds of di -
functionalization, including alkyl/oxycyanation, [13] carbonsulfonyl-
ation,[14] alkylarylation,[15] trifluoromethylation[16] and others [17] 
have been achieved, offering a convenient access to functional -
ized allenes. Particularly, the group of Liu [18] realized the rapid 
construction of CF3-containing allenyl nitriles using Togni reagents 
as the source of trifluoromethyl group (Scheme 1a). Besides, Bao 
and co -workers[19] reported the copper -catalyzed 1,4-fluoroalkyl-
cyanation of 1,3-enynes with LPO as oxidative additives, delivering 
a series of fluorinated allenyl nitriles (Scheme 1b). The above - 
mentioned approaches either rely on the use of Togni reagents, or 
require stoichiometric external oxidants, which may decrease the 
compatibility of functional groups. 
Given the high importance of fluorinated allenes and our   
Scheme 1  Synthesis of fluorinated allenyl nitriles via radical difunctionali-
zation of 1,3-enynes 
 
continuous interest in difunctionalization of 1,3-enynes under visi-
ble-light-mediated photoredox conditions, [20] we sought to inves -
tigate the possibility of a one -pot 1,4 -perfluoroalkylcyanation of 
1,3-enynes in a redox neutral form. Herein, we disclose a novel 
Cu/photoredox catalyzed three -component reaction under mild 
conditions, in which two new carbon -carbon bonds are stimulta -
neously formed via 1,4 -addition of perfluoroalkyl halides and 
TMSCN to 1,3 -enynes, furnishing structurally diverse perfluoroal -
kylated allenes in a highly chemo - and regioselective manner 
(Scheme 1c). 
Results and Discussion 
The addition of n-perfluoroalkyl io dide 2a and TMSCN to 
1,3-enyne 1a was selected as model reaction (Table 1). After a 
systematic investigation of reaction solvents, copper catalysts, 
ligands and photosensitizers (see the SI for details), the perfluoro -
alkylated allene 3a was isolated in 73 % yield when employing 
Cu(CH3CN)4PF6 as the catalyst, bpy as the ligand and Ir(ppy) 3 as 
the photosensitizer in DMAc under blue LEDs irradiation at room 
temperature for 12 h (entry 1). It ’s worth noting that the addition 
exhibited high chemo - and regioselec tivity, and no competing 
two-component cross -coupling byproducts, 1,2 -addition or 
3,4-addition byproducts were detected. When the amount of 
catalyst was reduced to 2.5 mol% Cu(CH 3CN)4PF6 and 3.5 mol% 
bpy, product 3a was obtained with a slightly decreased y ield (en-
try 2). As expected, control reactions omitting copper catalyst, 
ligand, photosensitizer or light indicated that each component 
was necessary for this cascade reaction (entries 3—6). A signifi -
cant erosion in yield was observed when the reaction w as con -
ducted in air atmosphere (entry 7).

With the optimal reaction parameters in hand, we explored 
the substrate scope of 1,3 -enynes (Scheme 2). The assessment 
started with electronic effects on the C2 -aromatic ring. The 
1,3-enynes bearing electron-donating (-OMe, -Me), electron-neu-
tral (-H) and electron-withdrawing substituents (-F, -Cl, -Br) on the 
para-position of benzene ring furnished the corresponding prod -
ucts 3a—3f with 68%—82% yields. The meta-position with meth-
oxy or methyl group could afford satisfactory yields ( 3g and 3h). 
To our delight, the ortho-position with methyl group also deliv -
ered the product 3i in 74% yield. Sterically demanding substrates 
could work smoothly as well, providing the products 3j and 3k in 
modest yields. With respect to the C2 -alkyl substituents, 
1,3-enynes embodying a cyclopropyl or methyl group were suc -
cessfully employed for th is reaction, albeit with lower yields ( 3l 
and 3m). The alkynyl moiety in the 1,3 -enynes was also investi -

gated. Linear alkyl chains with different lengths provided products 
3n—3q in 68%—86% yields. The branched alkyl group and benzyl 
substituent were prove n to be compatible as well, affording the 
products 3r and 3s in good yields. In addition, the system tolerat -
ed various functional groups, including chlorine, OTBS, cyclopropyl 
and a remote alkene function, giving the allene products ( 3t—3v 
and 3m) in acce ptable yields. The steric property of the alkynyl 
moiety had no obvious effects on the transformation efficiency 
(3w). Particularly, monosubstituted 1,3 -enyne at the 4 -position 
was a good candidate as well, affording the trisubstituted allene 
3x in 62% yie ld. Furthermore, when 1,3 -enyne possessing an in -
ternal alkene was employed, product 3y was isolated in 67% yield 
with modest diastereoisomeric ratio (5.2  : 1). Moreover, 
1,3-enynes bearing heterocycles such as pyridine , thiophene and 
1,3-benzodioxole were also successfully employed for the reaction, 
and the corresponding products were achieved in positive yields 
(3z—3ab). 
Scheme 2  Substrate scope with 1,3-enynesa 
 
a Standard conditions: 1 (0.2 mmol), 2a (0.4 mmol), TMSCN (0.4 mmol), 
Cu(CH3CN)4PF6 (5 mol%), bpy (7 mol%), Ir(ppy) 3 (1 mol%), and DMAc (1.0 
mL), under N2 at room temperature, 35 W blue LEDs, 12 h. Isolated yield. 
Then, we switched our attention to the scope of perfluoroal -
kyl halides.  As shown in Scheme 3, perfluoroalkyl iodides with 
different lengths, from perfluoropropyl to perfluorodecyl, were all 
well tolerated in the 1,4 -perfluoroalkylcyanation of 1,3 -enynes, 
providing the corresponding allenes 4a—4e in 62%—82% yields. 
Ethyl iodod ifluoroacetate could also participate in this transfor -
mation, affording difluoromethylene substituted allenes 4f and 4g 
in good yields. Notably, a comparable yield was obtained when 
using ethyl bromodifluoroacetate, a low-cost commercially availa-
ble raw material as the coupling partner . The relatively sterically 
hindered perfluoroisopropyl group could be installed as well, and 
4h was achieved in 70% yield. Additionally, the fluoroalkylating 
reagent bearing a terminal alkene group was well tolerated, albeit 
with a modest yield (4i), providing an additional handle for further 
functionalization. When 1,2 -dibromotetrafluoroethane was ap -
plied, a decreased yield was obtained ( 4j) and no diallenylation 
product was observed. To our surprise, tetrachloromethane wa s 
also a good candidate, furnishing trichloroallene product 4k in 
useful efficiency. It is worth noting that no allene products 4i and 
4k were obtained when the reaction was performed under the 
existing copper/peroxide system ,[19] which preliminarily demon -
strated the advantage of the mild copper/photoredox dual cataly-
sis.

To further demonstrated the practical utility of this transfor -
mation, gram-scale reactions were carried out under mild condi -
tions, affording the perfluoroalkylated allenes 3c and 3g in 55% 
and 50% isolated yields , respectively, with a small loss of efficien -
cy (Scheme 4). Subsequently, we conducted several control exper-
iments to gain more insight into the 1,4 -perfluoroalkylcyanation 
pathway. As shown in Scheme 5a, the reaction was completely 
inhibited when the radical scavenger TEMPO (2,2,6,6-tetramethyl- 
1-piperidinyloxy) or 1,1-diphenylethylene was added under the 
standard conditions, and the corresponding radical-trapping prod-
ucts 5a and 5b were obviously detected by GC -MS, indicating the 
involvement of the fluoroalkyl radical. In addition, ring -opened 
product 5c was obtained in a similar yield when 1,3 -enyne 1z and 
n-perfluoroalkyl iodide 2a were subjected to the reaction in the 
presence or absence of the copper catalyst (Scheme 5b). This 
observation supports that the fluoroalkyl radical was generated 
through photoreduction. More importantly, these results demon -
strate the existence of the propargylic radical intermediate, which 
was formed by fluoroalkyl radical addition and could deliver the 
allenyl radical via resonance. Finally, Stern–Volmer luminescence 
studies indicated that perfluoroalkyl iodides could quench the 
excited-state *Ir III efficiently, which demonstrated an oxidative 
quenching mechanism (see the SI for details).

According to the above studies and related literature  prece-
dents,[18,20a] a plausible mechanism for photoredox and copper 
dual catalysis is suggested in Scheme 5c. Upon irradiation of blue 
LEDs, the excitation of photocatalyst Ir(ppy) 3 leads to the active 
state A [Ir(ppy)3]* (E1/2III*/IV = ‒1.73 V vs SCE), which then under -
goes single electron transfer (SET) with perfluoroalkyl iodides (‒1.0 
to ‒1.5 V vs. SCE)[9] to afford fluoroalkyl radicals. The subsequent 
addition of the radical to the double bond of 1,3 -enyne generates 
the propargyl radical, which is in resonance with the allenyl radical. 
Meanwhile, Cu(I) species is oxidized by high -valence photosensi-
tizer B to afford Cu(II) species, which could react with TMSCN by 
ligand exchange. Then, the allenyl radical is captured to produce 
the allenyl copper(III) species C. Subsequent reductive elimination 
furnishes the perfluoroalkylated allene D and regenerate s Cu(I) 
species to complete the catalytic cycle. 
Conclusions 
In conclusion, we have developed a visible-light-induced 
1,4-perfluoroalkylcyanation of 1,3 -enynes via copper and photo -
redox dual catalysis, which points the way to streamline the syn -
thesis of functional perfluoroalkylated allenes. The reaction obvi -
ates the need for stoichiometric extern al oxidants and features 
mild conditions, broad functional-group tolerance, and exception-
al chemo - and regioselectivities, allowing for facile access to 
gram-scale reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies indicate 
that this transformation proceeds through a radical relay involving 
the resonance of the propargyl radical with the allenyl radical. 
Further studies of the detailed mechanism and additional applica -
tions of this protocol to synthesize fluorinated druglike molecules 
are ongoing. 
Experimental 
General procedure for the 1,4 -perfluoroalkylcyanation of 
1,3-enynes 
In a 10 mL sealed tube, Cu(CH 3CN)4PF6 (3.7 mg, 0.01 mmol, 
5.0 mol%), bpy (2.2 mg, 0.014 mmol, 7.0 mol%), and Ir(ppy)3 (1.3 
mg, 0.002 mmol, 1.0 mol%) were added in degassed DMAc under 
a nitrog en atmosphere, and the mixture was stirred at room 
temperature for 30 min. Then 1,3 -enyne (0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv), 
RfX (0.4 mmol, 2.0 equiv) and TMSCN (50 µL, 0.4 mmol, 2.0 equiv) 
were sequentially added. The reaction mixture was stirred for 12 
h in the pres ence of a 35 W Blue LED lamp (with a cooling fan to 
keep the reaction temperature at room temperature). After the 
reaction completion, the reaction mixture was diluted with EtOAc, 
then washed with brine, dried over MgSO 4, filtered, and concen -
trated under reduced pressure. The residue was purified by flash 
chromatography on silica gel to afford the allene products.
